title: HetEC: Architectures for Heterogeneous Quantum Error Correction Codes
problem: Surface codes for quantum error correction scale quadratically in physical overhead with the number of correctable errors, making them resource-prohibitive at scale. Quantum LDPC (qLDPC) codes offer superior scaling but lack a clear path to universal logical computation on their own; no architecture jointly exploits both code families.
motivation: Future fault-tolerant quantum computers need both resource efficiency and universal gate support, which no single QEC code provides, driving the need for heterogeneous multi-code architectures.
method: HetEC combines two complementary error-correction codes into a single quantum computer. Surface codes arrange qubits in a 2D grid and detect errors using physical geometry; they handle operations requiring magic state distillation (which enables the full set of quantum operations). qLDPC codes scale more efficiently for error correction. The architecture transfers error-corrected logical qubits between code regions and executes quantum gates remotely across boundaries through gate teleportation, enabling any quantum computation with fewer qubits than either code alone.
key_novelty: HetEC enables universal quantum computation by using surface codes for operations requiring magic state distillation and qLDPC codes for efficient error correction, combining their complementary strengths in a single architecture.
contributions: HetEC: a heterogeneous QEC architecture combining surface codes and qLDPC codes
Architectural design for universal logical computation across heterogeneous code boundaries
Analysis of resource trade-offs achievable by mixing code families
A clear path to universal logical quantum computation using qLDPC codes
limitations: Practical implementation challenges at code boundaries and overhead of logical qubit transfer not quantified in abstract.
primary_theme: heterogeneous quantum error correction architectures combining surface codes and qLDPC codes
